key_insight: A convex, iteration-dependent energy surrogate enables variational finite element schemes for anisotropic curve shortening with one-step energy dissipation.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports structure-preserving simulation of anisotropic interface evolution, including area-preserving flows.
method: Construct a smooth, convex surrogate that majorizes the anisotropic energy and matches it at the current iterate.
Minimize a time-step functional using parametric finite elements of any fixed degree.
Use convex splitting for strong anisotropy and a scalar constraint for area preservation.
evidence_signal: Numerical experiments show approximately expected convergence for smooth isotropic and weakly anisotropic cases, energy dissipation, and area preservation.
watch_item: Strong-anisotropy simulations develop mesh-scale oscillations under refinement; unique unconstrained steps also require a nonvanishing current curve derivative on every element.
paper_title: A minimizing-movement framework for parametric finite element approximation of anisotropic curve shortening flows
